item.title: Over 100 electric buses now operational in Frankfurt
item.dc:creator: Florian Treiss
item.description: In Frankfurt am Main, more than 100 buses are now either battery-electric or using fuel cells. Most recently, operator Transdev Rhein-Main (TDRM) has added nine electric buses from the struggling Dutch manufacturer Ebusco to its fleet.

item.title: Vandalism escalates at BYD Flash Chargers
item.dc:creator: Victoria Zippmann
item.description: BYD is increasingly falling victim to vandalism in China, with a photo of a chained-up Flash Charger now circulating on Chinese social media platforms. The perpetrator has not yet been identified and BYD has not commented on the incident. However, this is not the first bizarre incident involving a BYD Flash Charger.

item.title: Level 2 autonomy in urban areas: BMW announces driver assistant upgrade
item.dc:creator: Victoria Zippmann
item.description: Starting in 2027, BMW aims to expand its Level 2 assistant to urban traffic. For the first time, the system will also provide autonomous support during turning, in roundabouts, and at priority intersections. However, the driver must remain attentive and ready to intervene at all times. Pricing for the new features has not yet been announced.

item.title: Xpeng unveils mid-size SUV L05 – and announces Germany Launch
item.dc:creator: Victoria Zippmann
item.description: The Xpeng L05 is the Chinese brand's latest SUV and has already been unveiled in its home market. However, the manufacturer has now announced plans to bring the L05 to Europe and Germany. Xpeng intends to reveal further details at the Brussels Motor Show, which starts on January 8, 2027. Here is all the information we currently have about the Chinese version.

item.title: Janus Electric secures repeat order for six US electric truck conversions
item.dc:creator: Ciaran Daly
item.description: Australian truck repowering specialist Janus Electric has secured a repeat order from the California-based King Fio Trucking. The ~AU$3.1 million order comprises six Class 8 electric truck conversions and six JBS-650 swappable battery sets.

item.title: E.ON Next cuts overnight EV charging rate to 6.5p/kWh
item.dc:creator: Ciaran Daly
item.description: E.On Next has reduced overnight charging rates on its Next Drive Smart tariff from £0.08 / kWh to £0.065p / kWh. The energy supplier claims it is the lowest off-peak rate currently available on the British market.

item.title: Aberdeen’s ‘largest’ ultra-rapid EV charging hub enters operation
item.dc:creator: Ciaran Daly
item.description: Last month, RAW Charging opened a new 'ultra-rapid' EV charging hub on Palmerston Road in central Aberdeen, Scotland. The site features 14 charging bays, including four capable of delivering up to 300 kW power.

item.title: UK reviews cybersecurity requirements for public EV chargers
item.dc:creator: Ciaran Daly
item.description: The UK Department for Transport (DfT) has launched a consultation on proposed cybersecurity requirements for public EV charging points, which could lead to the establishment of a common minimum standard for chargers sold or installed across Britain.

item.title: Hanoi converts another bus route to all-electric operations
item.dc:creator: Ciaran Daly
item.description: Hanoi Transport Corporation (Transerco) has replaced its route 40 diesel fleet with a full electric range of electric buses - adding yet another electrified service to the Vietnamese capital's growing zero-emission public transport network.

item.title: Porsche appoints Jörg Bartels from Mercedes-Benz
item.dc:creator: Jasmin Apitzsch-Krause
item.description: Porsche is restructuring its development leadership. Starting in May 2027, Jörg Bartels will take over the Board of Management responsibility for Research and Development from Michael Steiner. The former Mercedes manager is set to lead technology realignment at the sports car manufacturer.

item.title: Webasto poised to sell its battery systems business
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: According to media reports, Webasto is seeking to divest its battery systems division. CEO Jörg Buchheim stated that the company is in advanced negotiations with two strategic investors. A deal could be finalised later this year. The proceeds would provide financial relief to the struggling supplier.

item.title: October: Chinese brands gain ground in Norway’s passenger car market
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: In Norway, 15,536 new electric cars were registered last month - a dominant 98.8 per cent share of all new passenger car registrations. This is primarily due to strong sales from Tesla and Toyota. However, Chinese brands are also gaining ground. Together, they already accounted for one-fifth of the market in the previous month.

item.title: Smart #2 limited edition sells out prior to market launch
item.dc:creator: Victoria Zippmann
item.description: The limited Couture Edition of the Smart #2 - Smart's electric successor to the Fortwo - sold out across Europe within 14 days. From Q2 of 2027, the 2.75-meter-long two-seater will hit the roads at a price of €19,990 euros.

item.title: Volkswagen explores vehicle production in Türkiye
item.dc:creator: Jasmin Apitzsch-Krause
item.description: Volkswagen is again considering car production in Turkey. To this end, the group has signed a letter of intent with its longstanding distribution partner Doğuş Otomotiv. The assembly of vehicles developed in China is also reportedly under discussion.

item.title: BYD achieves over 300,000 BEV sales in a single month for the first time
item.dc:creator: Florian Treiss
item.description: In October 2026, BYD sold over 300,000 pure electric vehicles in a single month for the first time. Globally, the Chinese manufacturer delivered over 490,000 vehicles, including plug-in hybrids. This represents an increase of around eleven per cent compared to October 2025.

item.title: SPIRIT-E project concludes that e-trucks can serve as mobile power banks
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: Electric trucks can not only charge using electricity but also store and discharge it selectively - like a power bank on wheels. This is demonstrated by the SPIRIT-E project after three years of research. The consortium has now presented the results of its joint work at a public online closing event.

item.title: LiveWire issues going-concern warning over business continuity risks
item.dc:creator: Jasmin Apitzsch-Krause
item.description: LiveWire has filed substantial doubts about its ability to continue as a going concern and is exploring options such as new financing, strategic partners, or a sale. Although electric motorcycle sales have recently increased, the Harley-Davidson spin-off's liquid assets have shrunk to just under $40 million.

item.title: GAC launches battery production in Thailand
item.dc:creator: Florian Treiss
item.description: Inpow Battery Technology, the battery division of Chinese automaker GAC, has started production at a new plant in Thailand. This expands the group's local manufacturing footprint in Southeast Asia.

item.title: Pennsylvania allocates $37m for more than 500 new EV charging ports
item.dc:creator: Ciaran Daly
item.description: The US state of Pennsylvania has announced a multimillion dollar investment in public EV charging infrastructure. This will fund 515 new charging ports across five counties as part of the federal NEVI programme.

item.title: Believ takes over 110+ EV chargers in Brighton & Hove
item.dc:creator: Ciaran Daly
item.description: UK charge point operator Believ has taken over more than 110 public EV chargers across 30 locations in the English city of Brighton & Hove. The chargers were previously operated by Blink Charging.

item.title: OEMs may have to take back EVs with faulty batteries
item.dc:creator: Florian Treiss
item.description: EU product safety law could provide buyers of electric cars with potentially defective high-voltage batteries an additional way to return their vehicles. The Offenburg Regional Court explicitly allows the reversal of the purchase in a case involving a Cupra Born based on the EU Product Safety Regulation.

item.title: Volkswagen pauses development of the ID.Golf
item.dc:creator: Jasmin Apitzsch-Krause
item.description: Volkswagen is temporarily pausing development work on the future ID.Golf. The automaker cites high cost pressure as the reason for the decision and plans to resume work as soon as the necessary investments can be secured.

item.title: E.ON acquires Smatrics EnBW Italia
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: After a two-year interlude, Smatrics EnBW is once again withdrawing from Italy and selling its four charging parks in the north of the country, to E.ON. The sites house a total of 64 fast-charging points. The purchase price is undisclosed.

item.title: Miele orders 840 electric transporters from Volkswagen Commercial Vehicles
item.dc:creator: Jasmin Apitzsch-Krause
item.description: Miele plans to expand its European service fleet with 840 battery-electric transporters from Volkswagen Commercial Vehicles. 440 vehicles are set to be deployed in Germany.

item.title: Allye introduces 400 kW fast charger with second-life batteries
item.dc:creator: Jasmin Apitzsch-Krause
item.description: British company Allye Energy has unveiled the MEV, a battery-buffered fast charger for depots. The system uses complete second-life batteries from EVs and is designed to provide up to 400 kW of charging power without necessarily requiring a more powerful grid connection.

item.title: Group14 to build battery material factory in Sagunt
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: US battery material manufacturer Group14, which specializes in silicon anodes, will in future also produce in Europe. The commitment to establish a production site in Spain is directly linked to a new capital increase - specifically, with a European investor.

item.title: Vingroup to build a €449-million EV plant in the Philippines
item.dc:creator: Ciaran Daly
item.description: In an effort to strengthen its footprint in the Southeast Asian auto market, Vingroup - the parent company of VinFast plans to build a new EV manufacturing facility in the Philippines. The Vietnamese conglomerate will invest US$500 million (approx. €449 million euros) in the new site.

item.title: Nio Firefly receives battery upgrade in China – with swap option for existing customers
item.dc:creator: Victoria Zippmann
item.description: Nio is granting the Firefly in China another upgrade. While the power output was increased in spring 2026, the focus is now on the battery and, consequently, the range. The manufacturer has announced an option for a 60 kWh battery. This battery has the same dimensions as the 42 kWh battery, meaning existing customers can also opt for a battery swap.

item.title: Rivian boosts revenue thanks to R2 and VW partnership
item.dc:creator: Florian Treiss
item.description: Rivian's revenue grew by 38 per cent in the third quarter of 2026 to $2.16 billion. Both the EV manufacturer's deliveries and its software and services business saw significant growth. 16 per cent of the revenue alone came from the partnership with Volkswagen. Rivian has also raised its annual forecast.

item.title: BYD plots new battery-electric coach launch in UK
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: BYD is set to battery-electric coach in the UK market by the end of the year, according to Frank Thorpe, BYD's Managing Director for Commercial Vehicle UK. The model is said to be specifically developed for the UK market.
